title: service-health-initiative-roadmap-and-cross-functional-sprints-2026-q3
content:
Purpose:
This document outlines a pragmatic, cross-functional roadmap to standardize Service Health objectives, implement early-stage SLOs for key inference surfaces, and run an initial 8-week sprint cadence with clear owners, checkpoints, and measurable success criteria. It is designed to be lightweight and actionable so teams can ship reliability improvements without adding heavy process overhead.

Context and why now:
- Platform growth (increased tenant count, spikes in hosted API usage, Dedicated pools expansion) has revealed gaps: inconsistent SLO definitions across teams, unclear error budget consumption signals, and uneven runbook coverage for model-serving incidents.
- Upcoming Dedicated capacity contracts and Private deployments require predictable latency and uptime targets for customer SLAs.
- Goal: create a repeatable approach that product, serving-runtime, infra, SRE, and product-ops can adopt to align on SLOs and incident readiness by end of Q3 2026.

High-level goals (outcome-focused):
1) Define and publish baseline SLOs for three service classes (Control Plane, Hosted API generation path, Embeddings) with associated measurement rules and alert thresholds.
2) Implement error budget windows and simple dashboards that are visible to product and SRE teams.
3) Run two cross-functional sprints that deliver runbooks, automated playbooks, and one rollback-capable rollout for a model-serving optimization (e.g., KV cache tuning or batching param change) with observability.
4) Create a lightweight governance cadence for SLO reviews and exceptions.

Scope (what's in / out):
In scope:
- Measurement instrumentation (metric names, tagging conventions) for service-level success and latency quantiles.
- Draft SLOs and SLI definitions, plus baseline evaluation for a 30-day window.
- Runbooks and post-incident checklist templates for the three service classes above.
- Dashboards and error budget alerts in NewRelic/Datadog.
- One test rollout (canary + auto-fallback) to validate rollback and incident response.
Out of scope:
- Full enterprise SLA contracting language (legal will be involved later).
- Large-scale infra re-architecture.

Principles (how we will work):
- Keep SLOs as business-aligned and simple as possible (no more than 3 per service class).
- Prefer pragmatic instrumentation over perfect coverage; iterate.
- Make ownership explicit: every SLO must have a service owner and an SRE partner.
- Automate alerting for error budget burn rather than relying on ad-hoc paging.

Proposed service classes and initial SLO candidates:
1) Control Plane (API for job submission, model metadata, rollouts)
   - SLI: success rate for control API calls (2xx) per minute, and p95 API response time for control requests
   - Candidate SLO: 99.9% success over 30 days; p95 latency < 250ms for aligned endpoints
2) Hosted Text Generation (frontend generation path used by public API endpoints)
   - SLI: generation request success (not an app-level error) and p99 token latency for generation step (inference kernel time)
   - Candidate SLOs: 99.5% success over 30 days; p99 generation latency < 1.2s for short prompts (<=128 tokens)
3) Embeddings Service
   - SLI: success rate and p95 latency for embedding vector return
   - Candidate SLO: 99.9% success over 30 days; p95 latency < 200ms
Notes: These are initial proposals — each service owner must validate feasibility with the serving-runtime team and product owners.

Metric & tagging conventions (minimum viable measurement):
- metric names: inference.requests.count, inference.requests.errors, inference.latency.ms
- tags: service=<service_class>, model=<model_name>, region=<region>, deployment_phase=<canary|stable|dedicated>
- Default window for reporting: rolling 30-day with daily snapshots and 12h error-budget alerts.

Success criteria (how we'll judge a successful 8-week program):
- All three service classes have published SLOs and SLIs with 30 days of measurement data.
- Error budget dashboard and two alert rules deployed to prod monitoring.
- Runbooks created for top 3 incident archetypes per service class and reviewed by SRE + service owners.
- One validated canary rollout with documented rollback within 60 minutes.

8-week sprint cadence (high level):
Week 0 (Prep, kickoff):
- Kickoff with product, serving-runtime, infra, SRE, and console teams.
- Align success criteria and pick the model or endpoint for the test rollout (owner: Lina Zhao).
- Create baseline metrics pipelines (owner: Miguel Torres).

Weeks 1-2 (Instrumentation & Baseline):
- Finalize SLI definitions and instrumentation changes for Control Plane and Embeddings.
- Implement tagging and metric collection.
- Build baseline dashboards for both services.
- Deliverable: dashboards + raw 7-day metrics (owner: Ben Carter).

Weeks 3-4 (SLO definitions & error budget tooling):
- Finalize SLO targets and SLO reporting queries (SRE + product sign-off).
- Configure error budget alerts: 12h burn alert, 24h burn escalation.
- Create a public SLO doc page for each service.
- Deliverable: SLO pages + alert rules (owner: Asha Patel).

Weeks 5-6 (Runbooks & Playbooks):
- Draft runbooks for the top 3 incident types per service class (e.g., model OOM, increased 5xx rate, region network partition).
- Create incident roles and escalation matrix.
- Run a tabletop incident drill with product and SRE.
- Deliverable: runbooks + drill notes (owner: Omar Haddad).

Weeks 7-8 (Canary rollout + retro):
- Execute test rollout (parameter change or model variant) with canary and auto-fallback enabled.
- Validate rollback procedure and measure time-to-recover.
- Post-release review and retro; update runbooks and SLO baselines.
- Deliverable: rollout report + action items for next iteration (owner: Priya Raghavan).

Key roles and responsibilities (RACI-lite):
- Service Owner: accountable for SLO acceptability and business alignment (product engineer).
- SRE Partner: owns measurement queries, instrumentation guidance, and alerting.
- Serving-runtime Lead: validates feasibility of kernel/latency expectations and provides performance data.
- Observability Engineer: implements dashboards and error-budget alerts.
- Incident Lead: coordinates tabletop drills and retros.

Initial owners (examples):
- Control Plane SLO owner: Miguel Torres (product infra)
- Hosted Gen SLO owner: Lina Zhao (serving-runtime)
- Embeddings SLO owner: Ben Carter (model infra)
- Observability: Priya Raghavan
- Incident lead / drill owner: Omar Haddad

Communication plan and meeting cadence:
- Weekly 30-min sync (Mon 9:30am PT) for sprint status and blockers.
- Bi-weekly SLO review every other Thu for leadership readout (30 min).
- Slack channel: #sre-service-health for async discussion and incident summaries.
- Public SLO pages will live in Confluence and link to dashboards.

Risk register (short):
- Instrumentation gap: metric missing at rollout -> contingency: ship with sampling and add fallback event-based checks.
- Alert fatigue: too many alerts for minor burns -> contingency: conservative thresholds, then iterate after two weeks of data.
- Ownership gaps across teams -> contingency: require explicit sign-off on each SLO and include a named backup.

Quick checklists (to keep momentum):
- [ ] SLI query reviewed by SRE and product owner
- [ ] Dashboard visible to product and SRE
- [ ] Error budget alerts configured and tested
- [ ] Runbooks reviewed in tabletop drill
- [ ] Canary rollback tested and documented

Next steps (immediate):
- Confirm kickoff attendees and send calendar invite (owner: Asha Patel) by EOD 2026-03-12.
- Select the model/endpoint for the rollout experiment (owner: Lina Zhao) by 2026-03-17.
- Miguel to publish baseline metric queries and a short how-to doc for instrumenting new endpoints (due 2026-03-20).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally lightweight — we want to iterate on SLO numbers after 30 days of telemetry. Please flag if any target is unrealistic; better to start conservative and tighten later.
- If your service cannot export the minimum tagged metrics quickly, call out the blocker and we will prioritize infra work in the first sprint.

Appendix: example SLI query snippets (pseudocode)
- success_rate = sum(inference.requests.count{service="hosted_gen",status=~"2.."}) / sum(inference.requests.count{service="hosted_gen"})
- p99_latency = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference.latency_ms_bucket{service="hosted_gen"}[5m])) by (le))

Action items (first cut):
- Asha: send kickoff invite, gather attendees.
- Miguel: push initial dashboards.
- Lina: pick canary target and confirm model variant.
- Priya: set up SLO pages in Confluence and link dashboards.
- Omar: coordinate tabletop drill schedule.

If anything in here conflicts with existing team plans, call it out in the kickoff — we will adapt. The intent is to create a repeatable minimum-viable SLO program that teams can adopt and extend into Dedicated and Private deployments in future quarters.
